item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.

item.title: China has formulated nearly 200 key standards for AI sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 -- China has so far formulated nearly 200 key standards for artificial intelligence (AI) to steer the sector toward sound and orderly development, an official with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) said on Wednesday. Xin Guobin, vice minister of the MIIT, told a press conference that AI has now been largely integrated across the entire chain in China, including research and development, design, production, manufacturing, quality inspection, as well as operations and maintenance. Multiple cities are being organized to carry out AI ethics review and service practices, Xin told the press conference held by the State Council Information Office. Liu Yulin, director of the information and communications development department of the MIIT, said at the press conference that during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), efforts to advance core 6G technologies will be accelerated. Continuous 6G technology trials and standards development will be carried out to promote the maturation of the 6G industry and the construction of its ecosystem, preparing for the commercial deployment of 6G, Liu said.

item.title: Chinese vice premier calls for joint efforts from APEC members to bolster food security
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
HANGZHOU, Aug. 25 -- China stands ready to work with all Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies to build a more stable food security system, Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong said on Tuesday. Liu, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks in a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 11th APEC Food Security Ministerial Meeting in Hangzhou, capital of east China's Zhejiang Province. Stressing the vital role APEC plays in safeguarding global food security, Liu called on APEC economies to jointly strengthen the foundation for food security by leveraging their own resource endowments. Liu proposed strengthening innovation-driven development and deepening cooperation in agricultural science and technology, while keeping trade flows smooth to safeguard the security and stability of food supply chains. He also called for stronger policy synergy to ensure food security. As a flagship event of the APEC "China Year," the meeting brought together around 200 delegates from the 21 APEC economies, the APEC Secretariat and other international organizations. It featured policy dialogues on agricultural and rural development, technological innovation and digital agriculture for food security.

item.title: Xi to attend SCO summit, pay state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 -- From Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan and President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi of Egypt, the Chinese foreign ministry announced on Wednesday. This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO. At the Bishkek Summit, Xi will have in-depth exchanges of views with participating leaders on deepening SCO cooperation in various fields under the new circumstances and major international and regional issues, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told a regular news briefing when asked for more information about the trip. They will provide guidance for the SCO's high-quality development and participation in the reform and development of the global governance system, Lin said. During his stay in Kyrgyzstan, Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations, cooperation in key areas, and international and regional situation with his Kyrgyz counterpart in their talks, and attend various state events, Lin noted. Lin said China looks forward to working with Kyrgyzstan to take this visit as an opportunity to promote high-quality development of mutually beneficial cooperation on all fronts, add new dimensions to the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, and bring more benefits to the two peoples. The Egypt leg of Xi's trip, his first state visit to the country in a decade, coincides with the 70th anniversary of bilateral diplomatic ties, the spokesperson said. The Chinese and Egyptian presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest, according to Lin. Through the visit, China looks forward to working with Egypt to carry forward traditional friendship, render each other firm support, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and bolster each other's modernization, thereby jointly drawing a new chapter of bilateral relations and contributing to regional and world peace and stability, Lin added.

item.title: Xi urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing after a mudslide in Nepal caused casualties at Gyirong border port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Wednesday morning. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called for efforts to evacuate residents at risk and provide timely medical treatment to the injured to minimize casualties. He made the instructions after a mudslide occurred at around 10:30 a.m. on Wednesday in Nepal, which caused severe casualties and left people unaccounted for at Gyirong border port in Gyirong County. Xi also stressed the need to strengthen monitoring and early warning, ensure scientific rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Noting that China is currently in a critical period of flood control, he urged local authorities and relevant departments to prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, fully implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention, and step up efforts to identify and address potential risks and hazards. He demanded resolute action to prevent major and catastrophic disasters and accidents and safeguard people's lives and property. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for an immediate verification of the number of the missing and affected people and for all-out rescue and relief efforts. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, instructed the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries, promptly share information and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, led officials from relevant departments to the site to guide rescue and disaster-response operations. Authorities in Xizang have mobilized forces to carry out search and rescue operations. All relevant operations are underway.

item.title: China's EV charging infrastructure expands rapidly in first seven months
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
BEIJING, Aug. 24 -- China's electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure has continued to expand swiftly, with the total number of charging points reaching 23.68 million by the end of July 2026, up 41.9 percent year on year, the National Energy Administration said on Monday. Of this total, public charging facilities numbered 5.099 million, an increase of 21.3 percent from a year earlier. Private charging facilities totaled 18.58 million units by the end of last month, surging 48.8 percent year on year. The data, sourced from the national charging infrastructure monitoring and service platform, highlights the continued expansion of China's EV support network alongside a surge in EV sales. China's new-energy vehicle (NEV) sales in July 2026 accounted for more than 60 percent of monthly new car sales for the first time, industry data showed earlier this month. In July alone, NEV output and sales reached over 1.57 million and 1.56 million units, respectively, up a respective 26.8 percent and 23.7 percent year on year, according to data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. As NEV sales continue to soar, China has been accelerating the improvement of its charging network to keep pace with growing demand. In October 2025, China unveiled a three-year action plan to improve the country's EV charging infrastructure, aiming to establish a nationwide network of 28 million charging facilities, with public charging capacity surpassing 300 million kilowatts by the end of 2027. China aims to increase the share of NEVs in its total vehicle fleet to 30 percent by 2030, according to an action plan for carbon peaking during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030).

item.title: Chinese premier meets Jordan's king
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
BEIJING, Aug. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing on Monday. Noting next year marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Jordan, Li said China stands ready to work with Jordan to carry forward the traditional friendship, enhance political mutual trust, firmly support each other on issues concerning each other's core interests, continuously deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and forge ahead together on the path to modernization. China is willing to strengthen development synergy with Jordan, jointly promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, boost bilateral trade, expand cooperation in science and technology and industrial innovation in fields like green energy, electric vehicles and the digital economy, and deliver more tangible outcomes, Li said. Li also called on both sides to step up cultural exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations, and steadily deepen mutual understanding and friendship between the two peoples. He said China is ready to work with Jordan and other relevant parties to make unremitting efforts to help de-escalate the situation in the Middle East and realize lasting peace and stability, expressing the hope that Jordan will continue to play an important role in the development of China-Arab relations. King Abdullah II said the Jordanian side firmly adheres to the one-China policy and recognizes that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory. Taking the 50th anniversary of Jordan-China diplomatic ties as an opportunity, Jordan stands ready to enhance exchanges with China at all levels, promote mutually beneficial cooperation in trade, investment, agriculture, mining, tourism and other fields, and explore cooperation in emerging areas such as renewable energy, scientific and technological innovation, and artificial intelligence, the king said. The king also noted that the Jordanian side firmly supports the four global initiatives put forward by China and looks forward to working with China to elevate Arab-China relations to a new level.

item.title: Xi calls on China, Jordan to further deepen alignment of development strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-24
BEIJING, Aug. 24 -- China and Jordan should further deepen the alignment of development strategies, Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Monday. Both sides should enhance cooperation in traditional fields including economy and trade, infrastructure construction, transportation and mining, expand new drivers of cooperation in digital economy, artificial intelligence and green energy, and comprehensively deepen exchanges in education, culture, science and technology, tourism and other areas, Xi said when holding talks with King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing. Xi noted that in 2015, the two heads of state jointly announced the establishment of China-Jordan strategic partnership, opening a new chapter in the development of bilateral relations. Facing an international and regional situation characterized by intertwined changes and chaos, building a more substantive and dynamic China-Jordan relationship is in line with the common expectations of the two peoples and also conforms to the general trend of the pursuit of the Global South for strength through unity, he said. Xi emphasized that China attaches great importance to Jordan's unique and significant role in the region, firmly supports Jordan in safeguarding its national sovereignty, security and development interests, and is willing to maintain close exchanges with Jordan at all levels including the governments, political parties, legislative bodies and localities, and enhance exchanges of experience in governance. China is willing to work with Jordan to implement the four major global initiatives, enhance coordination and cooperation in multilateral institutions including the United Nations, jointly safeguard the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order underpinned by international law, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said. King Abdullah II said Jordan and China have established a strong strategic partnership, with fruitful cooperation across various fields. He said Jordan firmly upholds the one-China policy and regards Taiwan as part of China's territory. Jordan places high priority on its relations with China and is dedicated to expanding cooperation and exchanges in economy and trade, manufacturing, agriculture, science and technology, pharmaceuticals, culture and education, King Abdullah II said, adding that Jordan welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest there to achieve common development and prosperity. Jordan speaks highly of the four global initiatives put forward by President Xi and looks forward to China's greater leading role on the global stage, King Abdullah II said. After the talks, the two heads of state jointly attended a signing ceremony for multiple cooperation documents in areas such as diplomacy, economy and trade, industrial and supply chains, and justice. The two sides also issued a joint statement on deepening the strategic partnership between China and Jordan. Prior to the talks in the Great Hall of the People, Xi held a welcome ceremony for King Abdullah II. Xi also hosted a welcome banquet for him in the evening.

item.title: Xi calls for stronger China-Ecuador synergy in development strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-19
BEIJING, Aug. 18 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday emphasized that China and Ecuador should strengthen the synergy of their development strategies and implement the cooperation plan for jointly building the Belt and Road. The two countries should deliver on cooperation projects in energy, minerals, infrastructure, finance and other sectors, and actively explore cooperation in areas including the digital economy, green development, new energy and artificial intelligence, Xi said when holding talks with President of the Republic of Ecuador Daniel Roy-Gilchrist Noboa Azín in Beijing. Noboa is on a state visit to China from Aug. 16 to 23 at the invitation of Xi. Noting this year marks the 10th anniversary of the China-Ecuador comprehensive strategic partnership, Xi said no matter how the international landscape changes, China has always viewed China-Ecuador relations from a strategic and long-term perspective. China stands ready to work with Ecuador to continuously elevate bilateral relations to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the people of both countries, he said. Xi said China respects and supports Ecuador in exploring a development path that suits its national conditions. China is willing to intensify exchanges between the two countries across various sectors, including governments, legislatures, and political parties, and enhance experience sharing on governance, he added. The Chinese president encouraged both sides to continue unlocking the potential of the free trade agreement so that its dividends can benefit more businesses and consumers. He also expressed China's willingness to cooperate with Ecuador in areas such as healthcare, poverty alleviation, disaster prevention and mitigation, in support of Ecuador's national development. Calling China an important partner and friend of Ecuador, Noboa said bilateral relations have entered a new phase, delivering tangible benefits to the two peoples. He said Ecuador is willing to deepen political mutual trust with China, supports China in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity, and respects China's position on the Taiwan question. Noting that Ecuador attaches great importance to cooperation with China, Noboa called on the two sides to strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation in economy and trade, finance, minerals, renewable energy, science and technology, culture and other fields. Ecuador will expand its exports to China, and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and operate in Ecuador, which is expected to help improve the well-being of the people and facilitate the development of the country, he added. The two heads of state exchanged views on the situation in the Latin American and Caribbean region. Xi said China supports Latin American countries in upholding independence and self-reliance, pursuing foreign cooperation based on their national interests, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. Xi stressed that China has always maintained that the status of the Latin American and Caribbean region as a zone of peace should not be undermined, the course of development and revitalization of Latin American and Caribbean countries should not be disrupted, and the right of Latin American and Caribbean countries to independently choose their cooperation partners should not be interfered with. Noting Ecuador highly values China's position and role, Noboa said Ecuador is always willing to be a good friend of China on the other side of the Pacific Ocean. After the talks, the two heads of state attended a signing ceremony for multiple cooperation agreements in areas such as green industry, economic and trade cooperation, the digital economy and people's livelihood. Prior to the talks in the Great Hall of the People, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Noboa. Xi also hosted a welcome banquet for him in the evening.
